description: resource-guard core dumps, for hook-parity: a core left by a crashed command gets an action to delete it, a core not tied to the command a keep-and-tell warn, and a reported core is not reported again. The hook reads the host's /proc/sys/kernel/core_pattern with no override, so what it prints depends on the host (a file pattern like `core` finds the files, a `|handler` pattern prints a handler note, simwin and non-Linux print nothing); the steps therefore check only the exit code, and the text is compared byte for byte by hook-parity.py on one host. The core is a 64-byte ELF header with e_type ET_CORE (program unknown)

steps.note: crashed (exit 139) and the core's program is unknown: delete it (action) when core_pattern writes files
a new core while a command that did not crash ran: keep and tell (warn); the first core is not reported again
a file named core that is not an ELF core is ignored
